description: Paths that the Step 4c state-drift gate (#2404) always protects. A sub-issue touching one of these requires the issue body to name the file explicitly under `Files to modify:` / `**Files:**`, or to carry a `Scope-Override: <reason>` line in the most recent commit message or an issue comment. A `### Files Changed` section does NOT satisfy this guard (#2788): Step 4c appends that section from the run's own commits before the gate reads the body, so counting it let a run license its own protected edits — the gate's input derived from its own subject. The union with `### Files Changed` still governs the `outside-declared-scope` violation class, where absorbing growth across passes is the intended #2520 behavior.

paths.reason: Per-project configuration; accidental edits break charter integrity and skill enforcement.
Versioned framework deployment contract; off-band edits desync dist + PHM consumers.
Schema-driven registries (extension points, recipes, criteria, signals); silent drift here breaks downstream consumers without test coverage.
Project-board configuration; accidental edits break GitHub Workflow integration.
Integrity seal for .gh-pmu.json; must only change when the config it seals also changes.
Project charter; out-of-scope edits drift from the project's stated vision and current focus.

registrarExemption.description: /work Step 4e runs register-helper.js, which necessarily edits framework-manifest.json and CHARTER.md. Neither is declarable when the issue is written, because the helper being registered does not exist yet. Before #2788 such runs passed only because the appended `### Files Changed` section absorbed them; with that absorption removed from the always-protected guard, this block is what keeps helper-adding runs from halting on paths the framework itself instructs the session to edit. EVERY triggerPattern must match at least one touched path before any exemptPattern applies. The co-occurrence requirement is the entire safeguard: touching a shared helper is ordinary work — #2788's own run edits scope-drift-check.js — so keying on that alone would re-open the hole this block accompanies. register-helper.js always edits constants.js, which ordinary helper work does not. An absent, malformed, or empty block exempts nothing: absence keeps the gate strict, the opposite polarity from a config whose deletion would silently disarm a guard. The exemption suppresses only the always-protected halt; the paths are still reported, and still raise advisory outside-declared-scope violations, so the run says what it did rather than passing silently.
